author: TheOnlyXeridian
quote:
X-Reviews:
This game gets a 1 strictly for its amazing graphics, and that is the only praise it deserves. From start to finish, the experience feels like a bait-and-switch that strips away the core identity of the Grand Theft Auto franchise. It takes six hours just to reach any real gameplay, and even then, the pacing never picks up. Instead of classic series staples, players are locked into mandatory relationship missions and unwelcome story beats that do a disservice to male protagonists, women, and military veterans alike. On a technical level, the game is a broken mess—ridden with severe bugs, broken AI, unresponsive NPCs, and abysmal frame rates that struggle to maintain 30 FPS on console. Worse yet, these major gameplay and performance issues were hidden until after launch, leaving players trapped past refund windows while outlets handed out glowing pre-release scores and early award nominations without real player input.

Positives:    
• Graphics: They did a great job on the Fidelity of the game, though this is what mainly hinders the frame rate until a PC version is released.    
• Sound & Music: This isn’t hard to get right these days and the music has some great selections from licensed offerings while the Composed music is serviceable.

 Negatives:    
• Bugs and glitches: Ridden with bugs throughout, including falling through the map, texture pop-ins, and flying through buildings without explosions or consequences.    
• Poor console performance: Struggles to hold a steady 30 FPS on any console, with lower-end consoles dropping to 10–15 FPS.    
• Slow pacing: Takes six hours to reach real gameplay and never picks up momentum.    
• Weak AI and NPCs: Features scripted, unconvincing AI and poorly coded NPCs, including unresponsive characters standing overnight inside closed stores.    • Shifted core mechanics: Reduces car theft and removes staple series elements such as sex workers and harming protesters.    
• Forced story and character direction: Locks players into mandatory relationship missions and unwelcome story beats, while main characters' faces closely resemble those from Red Dead Redemption 2.    
• Writing and representation: Criticized for its writing direction and for how it portrays women, military veterans, and male protagonists.    
• Refund and business practices: Accused of hiding rough gameplay until past refund windows, denying most refunds after launch, and facing fallout from firing 34 unionized employees in October 2025.    
• Critic scores and awards: Faulted for receiving perfect critic scores despite noted bugs, as well as eight pre-release award nominations before any player sentiment existed.    
• Price and MTX: Pushes the trend of raising base game prices to $79.99 while locking major pre-existing content behind a $20 Day 1 paywall, and even interrupts gameplay with an in-game pop-up pushing a GTA+ subscription for additional Day 1 exclusives.

Conclusion:
Ultimately, after 12 to 13 years of development and an estimated budget of $1 to $2 billion—making it the most expensive game ever produced—delivering an unpolished, bug-ridden product is inexcusable. Expecting players to simply accept a deeply flawed launch explains why so little real gameplay was shown prior to release and why refunds are being aggressively denied. When you spend over a decade and billions of dollars as a flagship AAA studio, players deserve a complete, functional, and faithful experience—not a broken game loaded with Day 1 paywalls.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND GTA VI, SAVE YOUR MONEY AND PLAY SOMETHING ELSE INSTEAD THAT DOESNT HOLD YOUR HAND , WASTE YOUR TIME, BELITTLE YOU AS A CHARACTER OR BAIT AND SWITCH YOU WITH SUBPAR GAMEPLAY.
